ky-jefferson-2026-soil-water-rooney-tyle.name: Tyler Rooney
ky-jefferson-2026-soil-water-rooney-tyle.bio: Student at Jefferson Community and Technical College and owner of a cleaning business.

positions.stance: Considers data centers "a direct environmental threat to Jefferson County" and will advocate against them.
Wants to help build Louisville's tree canopy with trees indigenous to Kentucky and educate the community about available programs.
Believes Louisville should invest more in flood prevention through stream and wetland rehabilitation and protection.

ky-jefferson-2026-soil-water-mayes-willi.name: William Donald Mayes
ky-jefferson-2026-soil-water-mayes-willi.bio: Retired Louisville resident who studied chemical engineering at the University of Louisville and interned with the U.S. EPA's Water Management Division.

positions.stance: Wants Louisville and Jefferson County residents and farmers to be more aware of the District's programs so they can take more advantage of them.
Will advocate for more funding for the District from Louisville Metro Government to expand its programs and community outreach.
Worries the Rubbertown hyperscale data center is on polluted land and could affect the water table; wants the District to help the community address these issues.

or-clackamas-2026-commissioner-pos2-shul.name: Mark Shull
or-clackamas-2026-commissioner-pos2-shul.bio: Retired Army lieutenant colonel and Marine veteran, former president of Shull Design and Development, elected Clackamas County Commissioner in 2020.

positions.stance: Pledges strict fiscal discipline, cutting government waste, property tax relief for seniors, and opposing all new taxes, including the Corporate Activity Tax.
Wants to stop tolling on I-205 "with no compromise."
Will oppose Metro's "overreach" and push land-use reforms that increase housing supply while preserving the rural economy.
Promises to listen to every resident, regardless of party, and put county families and taxpayers ahead of special interests.
Believes in "true equality of opportunity for all people, not divisive DEI mandates."

nv-clark-2026-assessor-warren-lynette.name: Lynette Warren
nv-clark-2026-assessor-warren-lynette.bio: Clark County homeowner in Mesquite and enrolled member of the Confederated Tribes of Siletz Indians.

positions.stance: Says new homeowners are sometimes defaulted to commercial rates; a fair assessor's office applies the correct residential rate from day one.
Wants assessment reviews to be "transparent, timely, and respectful" when taxpayers protest their assessment.
Says the assessor directly affects what residents pay to own a home and voters deserve someone who takes that impact seriously.

nv-clark-2026-recorder-borella-steven.name: Steven T. Borella
nv-clark-2026-recorder-borella-steven.bio: Has worked in customer service, sales, management, and the solar industry.

positions.stance: Calls recorded documents "the People's Records" and wants the office to remember it serves the people of Clark County.
Wants to expand awareness of the Recording Notification Service, simplify sign-up, and push for text alerts.
Will work to improve efficiency, strengthen oversight, support routine audits, and make the office easier to understand and use.
